objective.statement: Write scales with accidentals and recognise them with a key signature.
successCriteria: I can write a major scale with accidentals in front of the notes.
I know the same scale can be written with a key signature and no accidentals.
I can check a scale by its tone and semitone pattern.

explanation.text: There are two ways to write a major scale. You can put an accidental in front of each note that needs one, or you can use the key signature and write the notes plainly.

music.textAlternative: The scale of D major written with accidentals in front of F and C.

explanation.caption: With accidentals: the sharps are written in front of the notes that need them.

music.textAlternative: The scale of D major written with a key signature of two sharps and no accidentals.

explanation.caption: With a key signature: the same notes, with no sharps in front of them.

explanation.text: Both versions sound the same. In this course you will be asked which way to use, so read the question carefully.
To check a scale, say its letter names in order (each once), then check the semitones fall between notes 3-4 and 7-8.

music.textAlternative: The scale of D major written with a key signature of two sharps.

steps: Look at the two sharps at the start, on F and C.
Tap the scale: the F and C are sharp without any sign in front of them.
The same sound would be written with a sharp sign in front of both F and C if there were no key signature.
demonstration.textAlternative: The D major scale written with its key signature, each note linked to its keyboard key.

guided.prompt: Write the scale of D major, ascending, in the bass clef. Use accidentals instead of a key signature. The first note is written for you.
hints: One note on every line and space.
Semitones fall between degrees 3–4 and 7–8.
Major pattern: tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone.

mistakes.semitone-misplaced: Check the pattern of tones and semitones — the semitones aren't where they belong.
mistakes.letter-skipped-or-repeated: Each letter name appears once. You've used one letter twice and skipped another — respell that note.
mistakes.wrong-minor-form: Check which form of the minor scale is asked for, and which notes that form changes.
mistakes.melodic-descent-not-restored: Coming down, the melodic minor uses the notes of the key signature — undo the raised 6th and 7th.
mistakes.key-signature-misapplied: With a key signature, notes it covers don't need accidentals. Without one, every sharp or flat must be written.
mistakes.wrong-direction-or-octave: Check whether the question asks for ascending or descending, and which octave to start on.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Write one note per letter name first, then check the tones and semitones.

independent.prompt: Name the major key with this key signature.
hints: F♯ sits on the top line in treble and the fourth line in bass.
For sharps, the key is a semitone above the last sharp. For flats, it is the second-to-last flat (F major has one flat).

mistakes.wrong-count: Count again: each key has a fixed number of sharps or flats.
mistakes.wrong-order: Key signatures always follow the same order. Check which comes first.
mistakes.wrong-placement: The accidentals are right, but some are on the wrong line or space for this clef.
mistakes.relative-confusion: That key shares this key signature, but it's the relative key. Check the tonic.
mistakes.mixed-sharps-flats: A key signature uses only sharps or only flats.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Recall the order of sharps or flats and count how many the key needs.
